chunks: From him, from al-‘Abbās, from ‘Abd Allāh, from Rifā‘ah, from Abī ‘Abd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about one whose hand and foot are amputated: how does he perform wudu (ablution)? He said: “He washes that place from which it was cut.”

key_terms.الرِّجْلِ: the foot or leg, a limb discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الْأَقْطَعِ: a person whose limb has been amputated
key_terms.الْمَكَانَ: the place or area of the body
key_terms.الْيَدِ: the hand, one of the limbs relevant to wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: How does a person with an amputated hand or foot perform wudu (ablution) according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on how a person with an amputated hand or foot performs wudu (ablution). The Imam عليه السلام instructs that the person should wash the area from which the limb was cut, showing the application of ritual purity rulings according to one’s physical condition.
